title: AMC Global Media Streaming Revenue Rises 6% in Q2, U.S. Ad Sales Down 11%
description: AMC Global Media reported its second-quarter 2026 earnings Thursday on the heels of announcing a $500 million co-exclusive streaming deal with Netfl
body:
AMC Global Media reported its second-quarter 2026 earnings Thursday on the heels of announcing a $500 million co-exclusive streaming deal with Netflix for “The Walking Dead.”

	Streaming revenue for the second quarter, which ran March-May, increased 6% year over year to $180 million. 

	U.S. ad sales were down 11% at $109 million, with AMC noting that figure included “the one-time impact of a now resolved system integration issue in the second quarter” and excluding that factor “advertising revenue declined in the mid- single digit percent area.”
	

	In Q2, AMC Global says “restructuring and other related charges” came to $1.3 million, including a $800,000 charge due to its restructuring plan in its International segment and $500,000 related to severance charges.

	AMC has updated its full-year revenue forecast to between $2.4 billion-$2.5 billion based on the estimated impact of the new “The Walking Dead” licensing agreement with Netflix. Under the deal, AMC expects to receive a cash payment of approximately $25 million this year and annual cash payments of approximately $100 million in 2027, 2028, 2029 and 2030, and the remaining amount in 2031.

	Per AMC, “As a result of the extended payment terms, the aggregate revenue that the Company will recognize will be based on the present value of future payments, which is estimated to be approximately $445 million. In each of 2026 and 2027, the Company expects to recognize annual revenue related to the license agreement between $200 million to $225 million.”

	Currently, AMC Global Media’s streaming portfolio consists of AMC+, Acorn TV, Shudder, Sundance Now, ALLBLK, HIDIVE and All Reality. AMC’s linear networks include AMC, BBC AMERICA (which includes U.S. distribution and sales for BBC News), IFC, SundanceTV and We TV. The company also owns film distribution labels Independent Film Company and RLJE Films (which it acquired outright in Q4), and in-house studio AMC Studios.
	

	During its last quarterly earnings results in May, AMC said it will no longer report streaming subscribers on a regular quarterly basis moving forward. At that time, AMC said streaming subscribers had fallen 1% year-over-year to 10.1 million during the January-March quarter. AMC did not disclose a new streaming subscriber count for Q2 on Thursday.

	Overall, AMC Global Media’s domestic revenue fell 11% to $470 million in Q2. U.S. subscription revenue was down 5% ($306 million) and affiliate revenue dropped 17% ($126 million). Content licensing sales plunged 34% to $56 million.

	Turning to international operations, AMC saw subscription revenue tick down 1% ($46 million) while ad sales climbed 13% ($29.4 million) and content licensing rose 6% ($2.6 million). Total international revenue for Q2 was up 4% at $79 million.

	Wall Street forecast a loss of earnings per share (EPS) of 7 cents on $554.65 million in revenue, according to analyst consensus data provided by LSEG. AMC reported an adjusted loss per share of 28 cents on $547 million in revenue.

	“We are pleased to announce today an expansion of our relationship with a key long-term partner, Netflix,” AMC Global Media CEO Kristin Dolan said in a letter to shareholders accompanying the financial results. “We have reached a global co-exclusive licensing agreement for the streaming rights to the entire Walking Dead Universe, which will provide a meaningful source of cash flow for years to come. We renewed distribution agreements with major partners Comcast and YouTube. We are increasing our guidance for the full year as we leverage the value of our IP, the importance of our studio and the strength of our partner relationships, particularly in the area of distribution.”

schema.headline: AMC Global Media Streaming Revenue Rises 6% in Q2, U.S. Ad Sales Down 11%

title: Paul McCartney, Olivia Dean and Raye Make Mercury Prize Shortlist
description:
Paul McCartney has received his first-ever nomination for the U.K.’s prestigious Mercury Prize alongside Olivia Dean, Raye and more.

	The shortlist
body:
Paul McCartney has received his first-ever nomination for the U.K.’s prestigious Mercury Prize alongside Olivia Dean, Raye and more.

	The shortlist for the prize, which recognizes outstanding British albums, was unveiled on Thursday. Nominees include McCartney for “The Boys of Dungeon Lane”; Dean for “The Art of Loving”; Raye for “This Music May Contain Hope”; rapper Dave for “The Boy Who Played the Harp”; Irish singer-songwriter Dove Ellis for his debut album “Blizzard”; Florence + the Machine for “Everybody Scream”; pop star Jade for “That’s Showbiz Baby!”; jazz band Knats for “A Great Day in Newcastle”; hip-hop artist Kojey Radical for “Don’t Look Down”; drum and bass revivalist Nia Archives for “Emotional Junglist”; rock band Suede for “Antidepressants”; and the War Child charity compilation “Help(2),” which features Olivia Rodrigo, Arctic Monkeys, Cameron Winter and more. 
	

	Both Suede and Dave have formerly won the Mercury Prize in 1993 and 2019, respectively. Other recent winners include Sam Fender for “People Watching,” English Teacher for “This Could Be Texas,” Ezra Collective for “Where I’m Meant to Be,” Little Simz for “Sometimes I Might Be an Introvert” and Arlo Parks for “Collapsed in Sunbeams.”


	After artists submitted their music for the prize, the shortlisted albums were selected by a 12-strong jury, which this year included music broadcaster Afrodeutsche, jazz musician Jamie Cullum and The Times music critic Will Hodgkinson. The winner will be revealed at a prize ceremony in Newcastle on Oct. 22, with the victorious artist or band receiving a grant of £25,000 ($33,000).

schema.headline: Paul McCartney, Olivia Dean and Raye Make Mercury Prize Shortlist

title: George and Amal Clooney Evacuate French Home as Wildfire Threatens Brignoles: ‘We Remain Fully Part of This Community’ and Will ‘Contribute to Its Rebuilding’
description: George and Amal Clooney have evacuated their home in Brignoles in the South of France after a wildfire swept through the area, forcing hundreds of r
body:
George and Amal Clooney have evacuated their home in Brignoles in the South of France after a wildfire swept through the area, forcing hundreds of residents to flee.

	In a letter addressed to Brignoles Mayor Didier Brémond, the couple said they did not know whether their home — a hilltop estate called Domaine du Canadel — would survive the blaze but pledged to help rebuild the community.


	“We do not know whether our beautiful home will survive this terrible ordeal,” the Clooneys wrote. “As we evacuate Brignoles, we want to emphasize two things: We hope that you and the residents are safe. Amal and I are determined to ensure that, whatever happens to our village, we remain fully part of this community and contribute to its rebuilding. We love Brignoles and the friends we have there.”
	

	The fire burned through around 320 acres near Brignoles between Wednesday and Thursday, prompting the evacuation of roughly 600 residents and injuring four firefighters, according to Le Figaro. The blaze was brought under control thanks to the deployment of aerial firefighting aircraft alongside 270 firefighters and 70 vehicles, per the AFP.


	Firefighters remained on the ground Thursday morning working to secure the perimeter and extinguish hotspots before temperatures rise and southerly winds strengthen later in the day, Le Figaro reported, citing the prefecture of Var, where Brignoles is located. 

	Earlier this year, Clooney talked to Esquire magazine about his decision to move his family out of Hollywood after the birth of his twins, Alexander and Ella.
	

	“Yeah, we’re very lucky. You know, we live on a farm in France,” Clooney said. “A good portion of my life growing up was on a farm, and as a kid I hated the whole idea of it. But now, for them, it’s like — they’re not on their iPads, you know? They have dinner with grown-ups and have to take their dishes in. They have a much better life.”

	The Oscar winner and his family became French citizens in late December 2025, a move that sparked some controversy. A junior deputy to the interior minister, Marie-Pierre Vedrenne, suggested that Clooney had been granted French citizenship due to his fame rather than on merit and argued “this is not the right message to send.” Brémond, however, has welcomed the family’s presence in the region. 

	“I have dinner with them; they’re friends, not ‘celebrities.’ We can only be happy that they’ve chosen to live here,” the mayor told Le Figaro earlier this year.

schema.headline: George and Amal Clooney Evacuate French Home as Wildfire Threatens Brignoles: ‘We Remain Fully Part of This Community’ and Will ‘Contribute to Its Rebuilding’

title: Giorgio Armani Series in the Works From Fremantle-Owned Lux Vide and Iconic Designer’s Fashion House (EXCLUSIVE)
description: The life and career of Giorgio Armani is set to be the subject of a high-end TV series produced by Italy’s Lux Vide, which is collaborating with the
body:
The life and career of Giorgio Armani is set to be the subject of a high-end TV series produced by Italy’s Lux Vide, which is collaborating with the fashion house founded by the iconic designer known for his close ties to Hollywood.

	The still-untitled Armani biopic series — which will be tailored for the international market — has enlisted Turkish-born Italy-based director Ferzan Ozpetek, who is known for combining artistic depth with box-office appeal.
	

	Ozpetek, who knew Armani personally, recently scored a global hit with the 2025 crowdpleaser “Diamonds,” about a group of warm-hearted women in a Rome atelier rushing to fulfill a demanding order from an Oscar-winning costume designer client in the 1970s. “Diamonds” scored mightily at the box local office and traveled widely. Ozpetek’s TV experience includes 2022’s first Disney+ Italian original series “The Ignorant Angels,” a romantic drama spun off from his local hit “Ignorant Fairies.”


	“I knew, admired and spent time with Giorgio for many years, both on official occasions and in more private settings,” Ozpetek said in a statement to Variety. “We talked about cinema, of which he was notably passionate and an expert. But also about art, costumes, architecture, and, I would say, life itself. I could see within him a visionary and a brilliant artist. But also a down-to-earth and very determined man.”

	The director added: “The opportunity to tell his story is both an exciting honor and a challenge that involves capturing the many facets of such a complex, original and captivating personality.”
	

	Ozpetek is co-writing the screenplay for the Armani series in collaboration with Lux Vide’s head writer Francesco Arlanch, whose credits include Lux’s widely exported series “Medici,” “Hotel Costiera” and medical drama “Doc.” Storylines and series structure are being kept under wraps.

	Known globally as the Milan-based fashion pioneer with piercing blue eyes and a vision that combined laid back elegance and attention to detail, Armani first made his mark with the unlined men’s sports jackets and deconstructed suits worn by Richard Gere in 1980 in “American Gigolo.” But Armani also reimagined the woman’s power suit. He dressed scores of Hollywood’s female stars including Julia Roberts, Diane Keaton, Jodie Foster, Cate Blanchett, Lupita Nyong’o, Anne Hathaway and Michelle Yeoh in both minimalist attire — such as the Armani men’s suit famously worn by Julia Roberts when she won a Golden Globe for “Steel Magnolias” in 1990 — and glittery gowns like the “Nairobi blue” crystal-encrusted sequin gown worn by Lupita Nyong’o at the 2024 Academy Awards. The long list of male actors who regularly wore Armani on red carpets, and also on screen, comprises Leonardo DiCaprio, George Clooney Russell Crowe, Robert De Niro and Tom Cruise, to name a few.  

	His Hollywood connection earned Armani wardrobe film credits in more than 200 movies. 

	Armani — a self-made man who fully owned his $10 billion fashion empire at the time of his death on Sept. 4, 2025 at age 91 – was known to often appear in dark trousers and his trademark black T-shirt. He was born in the northern Italian town of Piacenza on July 11, 1934. After two decades in the fashion industry starting in 1957, he and his partner Sergio Galeotti sold their Volkswagen for $10,000 to start up their own menswear ready-to-wear label. They launched both men’s and women’s lines the following year.

	Fiercely private, Armani rarely discussed his personal life. He did tell Vanity Fair that he had romances with both men and women. He was in long-term relationship with Galeotti until his AIDS-related death in 1985.

	The Giorgio Armani fashion house has agreed to support production of the Fremantle TV series, providing access to its “archives, creations and iconic locations, offering an unparalleled insight into the world and legacy of one of fashion’s most influential figures,” according to a Fremantle statement.
	

	“For years, Lux had been chasing the dream of telling the world the story of Giorgio Armani, an artist who invented a unique and recognizeable style,” Lux Vide founder and president Matilde Bernabei said in a statement. She went on to describe Armani as “a standard-bearer of Made in Italy who rewrote the rules of style and elegance.”

	“It will be an ambitious series,” Bernabei added, “and we are proud to know that the market has immediately embraced this project with interest, enthusiastically confirming its international potential.”



	

					Giorgio Armani and Ferzan Ozpetek
									Stefano Guindani/Courtesy Armani

schema.headline: Giorgio Armani Series in the Works From Fremantle-Owned Lux Vide and Iconic Designer’s Fashion House (EXCLUSIVE)

title: Italy-Based Lights On Snags Colombia’s ‘In All My Journeys I Am Returning’ Ahead of Its Locarno Bow (EXCLUSIVE)
description: Boutique Italian sales agency Lights On has picked up international sales rights to the debut feature of Colombian Manuel Ponce de León’s “In All My
body:
Boutique Italian sales agency Lights On has picked up international sales rights to the debut feature of Colombian Manuel Ponce de León’s “In All My Journeys I Am Returning” (“Todos mis viajes son viajes de regreso”) ahead of its world premiere at the Locarno Film Festival.

	“It’s an exceptionally bold and distinctive first feature film that we’re confident will resonate with audiences around the world,” said Flavio Armone, co-founder & managing director at Lights On, who expressed the company’s delight at returning to Locarno’s Filmmakers of the Present competition for the fifth consecutive year. 
	

	“This film has been a long and deeply personal journey and I am very happy to have found a team that understands its sensibility and the spirit in which it was made,” said Ponce de León, who studied filmmaking in Berlin aside from art history and philosophy in Colombia.


	Set in early 19th-century Colombia, “Journeys” follows a young Swedish couple as they navigate up the Magdalena River in search of a fabled gold mine. As they drift through a war-scarred landscape, time fractures, memory overtakes reality and history becomes fluid. Their voyage transforms into a haunting meditation on exile, longing and the elusive promise of belonging.

	Ostensibly, Ponce de León’s studies in philosophy inform his work as does his interest in poetry and particularly that of Colombian 20th century poet León de Greiff whose line ‘All journeys are journeys of return’ has haunted him since his childhood.

	Poetry and rivers run through his feature debut as they do in his two previous short films.
	

	“The figure of the river is an element that, at first, I wasn’t even consciously aware of. It was very intuitive, until one day a colleague asked me, ‘Why is there always a river? What’s the story with the river?’ And I thought, ‘Wow, that’s true—I hadn’t realized it,’” he told Variety.

	“There is clearly a recurring presence of the river: the river as a space of memory, as a place where different times converge, almost like a path or a vehicle through time itself,” he explained.

	“My father is a poet and I think poetry has always been present in my work as well. So, poetry and literature have always been part of my creative universe. They continue to be a source of inspiration and a way of approaching cinema.”

	He shot his drama, filmed in evocative sepia tones by his long-time collaborator Angello Faccini, along Colombia’s Magdalena River, which was a fundamental commercial trade route throughout the country’s history. The colonial-era town of Honda, known as the City of Bridges due to its more than 40 bridges, was his base. “The short film I made before this one, ‘Beyond the Night,’ was filmed on the banks of the river, very close to Honda. I don’t really know why I’ve ended up making so many projects in Honda—I’ve developed a very strong creative relationship with the place.”

	Finding his Swedish actors was serendipitous and as extraordinary as his story. As he cast his net across social media and other means, he heard from a Camila Bejarano Wagner who wrote that she was Swedish but with a Colombian mother and that she’d be visiting her grandmother In Colombia so she could audition then.

	“During her stay, Camila was living with her aunts in Colombia. They asked her what the film was about and she explained that it was inspired by the poet León de Greiff—a name she herself hadn’t known before. That’s when her aunts told her something extraordinary: the grandmother she had come to visit had once been de Greiff’s lover,” he related. “Camila ended up discovering postcards and handwritten love letters signed by de Greiff himself—remarkable letters addressed to her grandmother. There were also personal keepsakes, including the Scrabble set de Greiff had given her, the very one they used to play together.”
	

	However, what really drew Ponce de León to Camila wasn’t just her story, but what she brought to the role. “Nostalgia is one of the film’s central themes—it lies at the heart of the characters’ emotional conflict. From the very beginning, I felt that, although Camila had been raised in Sweden her entire life, she carried a deep longing for her Colombian roots. She was intensely curious and genuinely eager to reconnect with her mother’s Colombia, with that distant part of her own past. That made her an especially compelling fit for the character.”

	To find Camila’s counterpart, Fredrik Lundin, Ponce de León met him in Stockholm after having traveled to a tiny village called Gunnarskog, north of the Arctic Circle, where every year, the village hosts a festival in honor of de Greiff and one of his fictional alter egos, Gaspar de la Noche. “It’s a remarkable thing—a remote Swedish village celebrating a Colombian literary figure.” Renowned French indie actor Denis Lavant plays a pivotal role in the film where the dialogue is in Spanish, Swedish, French and Polish.

	“In All My Journeys I Am Returning” is produced by Ponce de León’s Los Niños Films with Daniela Rocha Giraldo, Ana Winograd and Héctor Ulloque producing alongside him.

	The 79th Locarno Film Festival runs over August 5-15.

title: ‘Ramayana’ Trailer: Ranbir Kapoor and Yash Face Off in First Part of Nitesh Tiwari’s Epic
description: The first trailer for “Ramayana” has debuted, marking the most substantial promotional asset yet for Nitesh Tiwari‘s two-part adaptation of the anci
body:
The first trailer for “Ramayana” has debuted, marking the most substantial promotional asset yet for Nitesh Tiwari‘s two-part adaptation of the ancient Hindu epic, ahead of a worldwide release this November.

	The story follows exiled prince Rama (Ranbir Kapoor) and his consort Sita (Sai Pallavi) through exile into catastrophe, as Sita’s abduction at the hands of Ravana (Yash) sets in motion an epic war between righteousness and evil. Part 1 is expected to culminate with the abduction itself, leaving the rescue campaign and the climactic battle for Part 2. Both parts are filmed for Imax.  The two films together are budgeted at approximately $500 million, Variety understands.
	

	The long-awaited trailer offers a sweeping first look at the Hindi-language spectacle, which will also be dubbed into several other languages. 


	The preview opens with an introduction to demon king Ravana asserting his dominion across the three realms of heaven, earth, and the underworld. A voiceover establishes the overarching mythological conflict, explaining how Lord Vishnu takes human form to restore righteousness on earth when chaos threatens the universe, introducing Kapoor’s Prince Rama as King Dasharatha’s (Arun Govil) eldest son.

	The trailer shifts focus to Rama’s 14-year exile to the forest to uphold his father’s vow, accompanied by his wife Sita and brother Lakshmana (played by Ravi Dubey). The peaceful exile is shattered when Ravana’s sister, Surpanakha (played by Rakul Preet Singh), becomes infatuated with Rama, setting off a chain of events that leads to her humiliation. Vowing retribution, Ravana steps in to restore his pride, initiating the conflict that leads to Sita’s abduction.
	

	Building to a grand finale, the footage showcases high-scale visual effects, mythological weaponry, and massive army battles as Rama vows to defeat Ravana across the three worlds and rescue Sita, signaling the start of the era of Rama.

	The film is produced by Namit Malhotra’s Prime Focus Studios and Yash’s Monster Mind Creations.

	Kapoor, Yash, Tiwari and Malhotra, founder of Prime Focus and DNEG CEO, appeared at San Diego Comic-Con to debut the new clip and discuss the making of the epic movies.

	“Ramayana” Part 1 is set to open during the Diwali holiday frame, with Part 2 following on Diwali 2027. The choice of release window is no accident. Diwali – one of the most widely observed festivals in the Hindu calendar – marks the return of Rama to his kingdom of Ayodhya after 14 years of exile and his victory over Ravana. The lighting of lamps that defines the celebration is said to represent the illumination of Ayodhya on the night its beloved prince came home.

	Score duties are shared by Oscar-winning composers Hans Zimmer and A.R. Rahman. DNEG – the eight-time Oscar winning VFX house, whose credits include the “Dune” movies, “Interstellar” and “Inception” – is handling visual effects. Tiwari, whose “Dangal” remains the highest-grossing Indian film ever made, directs from a screenplay by Shridhar Raghavan.

	Sony Pictures is handling international distribution for all territories outside India and Dharma Productions within India.

title: San Sebastián New Directors: Billy Lumby, Marlene Emilie Lyngstad, ‘Money Heist’ Star Jaime Lorente and More
description:
BAFTA nominee Billy Lumby and Norway’s Nordic Talents winner Marlene Emilie Lyngstad will compete at San Sebastian’s New Directors strand.

	Also in
body:
BAFTA nominee Billy Lumby and Norway’s Nordic Talents winner Marlene Emilie Lyngstad will compete at San Sebastian’s New Directors strand.

	Also in the mix is “Erratics,” starring Denis Lavant. a Chile-France-Argentina co-production directed by Thomas Woodroffe.

	One of the most prestigious new talent spreads in Europe, New Directors will open with “The Bad Son” (“El mal hijo”), the debut feature film as a director of “Money Heist” star Jaime Lorente, and close with Lumby’s “Florid,” which marks the feature debut of Lumby, whose second short, “Samuel 613,” was nominated for a BAFTA, 
	

	As a project, “Cute” won the Nordic Talents top prize at Cannes, Its Norwegian director Marlene Emilie Lyngstad and Danish producer Carl Olsbæk Adelkilde hace already made the joint graduation film “Norwegian Offspring” which scooped Cannes La Cinef first prize and Haugesund’s Next Generation Award marking them out as talent to track.


	Of New Directors titles announced July 30, there’s also good word on Ayana Nurdinova’s “Mugalim,” from Kazakhstan burgeoning film scene, produced by Kazakh Cinema and Art East Films, and “Morro,” a Mexican small town set tale of grief and unlikely friendship. 

	 San Sebastián’s just announced New Directors entries join three Spanish features announced on July 17: Javier Giner’s “Esa Soledad,” a portrait of Millennial existential emptiness; El mal hijo,” directed by “Money Heist” star Jaime Lorente, and “February, Seven Days,” (“Sieben Tage Februar,”), from Tatjana Moutchnik, a family drama unfolding on the eve of Russia’s invasion of Ukraine. 
	

	These are the titles selected for the New Directors sidebar at this year’s San Sebastián Film Festival:

	“The Bad Son” (“El mal hijo,” Jaime Lorente, Spain) – Opening FilmCast: Miguel Ángel Puro, Susi Sánchez, Hugo Arbués, Óscar de la Fuente

	The first feature as a director of Lorente, Denver in “Money Heist,” adapting a novel by Salvador S. Molina, a screenwriter on Bambú productions such as “Jaguar” and “13 Exorcisms.” Set in Murcia, a coming of age tale in which a half gitano boy is abandoned by his father, goes to live with his grandmother, who has kidnapped his father. Produced by Frank Ariza at AF.  



	

									‘The Ballet Lesson’ Courtesy of San Sebastian Film Festival
	



	“The Ballet Lesson” (Kazuya Murayama, Japan)Cast: Vadim Bushmakin, Nikita Kondo, Niina Kondo, Yukina Shimizu

	Murayama follows his 2021 debut, “Torao,” with a family journey centred on Japanese-Russian siblings Nikita and Nina. Raised by their Russian grandparents in a provincial Japanese town, the children know their absent parents largely through stories. When their father, Nikolai, suddenly returns, he takes them to see their mother, Yuki, a Japanese ballet dancer. Along the way, unfamiliar landscapes and brief encounters reveal the fragile bonds holding their divided family together again.

	“Erratics” (“Bloques erráticos,” Thomas Woodroffe, Chile-France-Argentina)Cast: Denis Lavant, Daniel Muñoz

	Freed from the Patagonian tundra, ad played by Lavant, the spirit of filmmaker Lucien Castlenau – a reference to Paul Castelnau and Lucien Le Saint, director of 1926 hit “Voyage à la Terre de Feu” – wanders through a futuristic Patagonia. The top winner at Rotterdam’s 2025 Cinemart from Bloques Erráticos La Belle Affaire Productions and Un Puma, positing ghosts as memories, and questioning who owns historical memory.  

	“Florid” (Billy Lumby, U.K.-Sweden) – Closing FilmCast: Jonathan Jules, Saskia Chana, Unknown T

	Social issue genre: Jamal in a London of “supported accommodation and psychiatric wards,” hears voices, battles psychotic breakdown, takes medication, aims to make it in music, has his frail balance rocked when Kyla moves in next door. Backed by BBC Film and Film4, part of the BFI’s Cannes Great 8 showcase, produced by Atar Studio and Film i Väst and sold by Atar.  
	

	“Body of Glass” (Naëmi Ada, Germany-France)Cast: Soma Pysall, Elise Tilloloy, Manuel Severin, Younès Boucif

	German filmmaker Ada draws on her contemporary dance training for her feature debut, following dancer Tian after a violent incident with her controlling partner, Felix. Fleeing their Marseille life, she infiltrates the grieving cycle of a dead young man by posing as his secret girlfriend. As mourning, affection and deception intertwine, Tian conceals a truth: Felix remains tied captive in their apartment, forcing her to confront whether she can break the cycle.

	“Cute” (Marlene Emilie Lyngstad, Denmark-Sweden-Norway)Cast: Jan Gunnar Røise, Gina Jaqueline, Karin Bertling, Kitt Maiken Mortensen

	Backed by Nordisk Film, Cannes project winner “Cute” turns on a mass produced stuffed animal that links different human destinies in what has been described as a “global tale about the longing for innocence in a world filled with guilt and an “exploration of the grotesqueness and the tenderness in the human desire for “the cute.”  

	“February, Seven Days” (“Sieben Tage Februar,” Tatjana Moutchnik, Germany-Austria-Spain)Cast: Serhii Korshykov, Volodymyr Holosniak, Maria Shtofa, Arsenii Markov

	German-Ukrainian filmmaker Tatjana Moutchnik makes her feature debut with a family drama unfolding on the eve of Russia’s invasion of Ukraine. A man from Odesa travels with his son to Stuttgart for his mother’s funeral, reuniting with an estranged brother as competing ideas of family collide. The project won San Sebastián’s WIP Europa Industry Award and WIP Europa Award in 2025.

	“Lovers Sleep Alone” (Massih Parsaei, Germany)Cast: Pooyesh Frozandeh, Ava Darvishi, Marcel Kohler, Wolfgang Wobéto

	Selected for San Sebastián’s WIP Europa in 2025, Parsaei’s feature debut centres on Iman, an Iranian exile who has built his Berlin life around absence: from family, homeland and intimacy. He fills the silence with work, inventing stories and encounters with a man he meets for sex in a park. When a barely known cousin arrives from Tehran, the world Iman abandoned quietly begins finding its way back into his constructed existence.

	“Morro” (Rodrigo García Saiz, Mexico)Cast: Gustavo Sánchez Parra, Anna Diaz, Ernesto Meléndez
	

	Mateo, a small-town vet, is called in to tend Morro, the local cartel leader’s injured dog. Through this simple act of care, he begins to return to life. “‘Morro’ was born out of a need to look closely at an environment where violence has become part of everyday life” focusing on what remains after it: the silences, the bodies that continue inhabiting the world, and the relationships that endure despite loss,” says García Saiz (“Lluvia”).

	“Mugalim” (Ayana Nurdinova, Kazakhstan)Cast: Oljas Dalelkhan, Rustem Zhanyamanov, Shynar Janysbekova, Olga Landina

	From Kazakhstan burgeoning film scene, produced by Kazakh Cinema and Art East Films, the tale of a music teacher who dreams of leaving the small town of Balkhash, who is suddenly given the chance to leave. He hesitates, however. The debut feature of Yurdinova, who has worked as a production designer and direction assistant.

	“My Father’s Shoes” (“Obuvkite na bashta mi,” Hristo Simeonov, Bulgaria-France)Cast: Valeria Varbanova, Tanya Shahova, Vyara Kolarova

	Bulgaria’s Simeonov makes his feature debut with a mother-daughter drama rooted in absence and pain. Mima has grown up without her father, raised by her uncompromising mother, Boyka. When news of his death arrives and his body is returned to their village, identifying him becomes both a duty and a  dilemma. Boyka refuses to confront the man she once loved, leaving Mima to decide what it means to inherit the life she never chose.

	“This Solitude” (“Esta soledad,” Javier Giner, Spain)Cast: Oriol Pla, Marina Salas, Gemma Martínez, Kai Etxaniz, Itziar Lazkano

	Giner’s feature debut, once more partnering with star Oriol Plá. here with Marina Salas (“El Barco”), in a portrait of Millennial “existential emptiness in a fragmented and chaotic present,” Giner has said. Sold by Filmax and produced by Fuga de cuerpos, A.I.E., Balance Media Entertainment, La Embajada TV and  Basajaun Filmak.



	

									‘Will You Still Be My Friend’ Courtesy of San Sebastian Film Festival
	



	“Will You Still Be My Friend” (“Ri Guang,” Lu Po-Shun, Taiwan-Singapore)Cast: Jaden Wang, Aloysius Looi, Lung Tien Hsiang, Lu Yi-Ching, Andie Chen

	Set amid an escalating feud in a rural Taiwanese village, Lu Po-Shun’s feature debut follows a boy trying to protect his secret friendship with his Singapore-raised best friend. As conflicts among the adults threaten to pull them apart, he begins quietly questioning the true nature of his feelings. The film turns a hostile community into the backdrop for an intimate story about loyalty, emotional discovery and a relationship placed under mounting pressure.
	

	“The World Before” (Yoon Dan-bi, South Korea-Japan-France)Cast: Su-bin Sim, Eo-jin Kim

	After winning several awards at Busan and Rotterdam with her debut, “Moving On,” which screened in San Sebastián’s Perlak section in 2020, Yoon Dan-bi returns with her second feature. Seventeen-year-old Jin has never left the remote island where she was born. When Dujae arrives for his grandmother’s funeral, an unexpected intimacy develops between them, gradually transforming Jin’s perception of the island, its quietly familiar rhythms and herself as summer draws toward its close.

title: ‘The Walking Dead’ Franchise to Stream on Both Netflix and AMC+ Beginning in 2027 Under New $500 Million Deal
description: AMC Global Media‘s “The Walking Dead” franchise will stream on both Netflix and AMC+ beginning in 2027 as part of a new five-year, $500 million lice
body:
AMC Global Media‘s “The Walking Dead” franchise will stream on both Netflix and AMC+ beginning in 2027 as part of a new five-year, $500 million licensing deal.

	The co-exclusive global licensing pact between Netflix and AMC Global Media covers the original “The Walking Dead,” as well as all six of its spinoffs, including “Fear the Walking Dead,” “The Walking Dead: Daryl Dixon,” “The Walking Dead: Dead City,” “The Walking Dead: The Ones Who Live,” “The Walking Dead: World Beyond” and “Tales of The Walking Dead.” In total, that’s 371 episodes.
	

	Licenses for each series will begin on different dates in different geographic territories, following the expiration of existing streaming licenses, per AMC.


	Netflix has held the exclusive U.S. streaming rights for “The Walking Dead” since 2011. The new deal will allow AMC+ to stream the main series for the first time ever, and extend the show’s availability on Netflix the U.K., Italy, Australia and New Zealand, among other territories.

	“Audiences have discovered and loved The Walking Dead on Netflix for nearly 15 years and the show continues to attract new fans,” said Lori Conkling, Vice President of Licensing at Netflix. “We’re excited to partner with AMC Global Media to continue to expand that access to more audiences around the world and bring the entirety of The Walking Dead Universe to Netflix.”

	“We are thrilled to expand our long-time partnership with Netflix around The Walking Dead,” said Kristin Dolan, CEO of AMC Global Media. “This deal creates a global destination for this universe – all shows, all episodes – making the franchise more accessible than ever to fans around the world. In addition, the co-exclusive agreement allows us to bring the original series to AMC+ for the first time early next year. Netflix has been an important partner in making The Walking Dead one of the most successful franchises in the history of entertainment. This agreement is a fantastic result for our companies, for the fans and for this timeless IP.”

schema.headline: ‘The Walking Dead’ Franchise to Stream on Both Netflix and AMC+ Beginning in 2027 Under New $500 Million Deal

title: Ryan Bingham Signs With WME (EXCLUSIVE)
description: Singer-songwriter-actor and “Yellowstone” star Ryan Bingham has signed with WME for worldwide representation in music, the company announced on Thur
body:
Singer-songwriter-actor and “Yellowstone” star Ryan Bingham has signed with WME for worldwide representation in music, the company announced on Thursday. He continues to be represented by Jack Whigham at Range Media Partners for film and television.

	Bingham has had a remarkably versatile career that stretches back nearly 25 years. He released his indie debut album, “Wishbone Saloon,” in 2002 and his major-label bow, “Mescalito,” five years later. But he broke into the national consciousness in 2010 by co-writing and performing two songs on the soundtrack for the hit film “Crazy Heart,” including the song “The Weary Kind,” which earned him an Oscar, a Grammy, a Golden Globe and a Critics’ Choice Award. He was named Artist of the Year by the Americana Music Association the same year. 
	

	He has released albums steadily, but his star rose again in recent years with his recurring role as the ex-con and singer Walker on Paramount’s “Yellowstone.” His original music, including the track “Wolves” from his album “American Love Song,” has been heavily featured on the show.


	Last May, Bingham released “They Call Us the Lucky Ones,” his first full-length album with his backing band the Texas Gentlemen, and hit the road for his headlining Still Gettin’ Away With It Tour ‘26, which ran through June. After a few festival performances, he will finish the summer supporting Zach Bryan on stadium dates in San Diego, Salt Lake City, Denver, and Glendale, AZ, starting later in July; he supported Bryan last September at his massive concert at Michigan Stadium, which drew an audience of 112,408 — setting the record for the largest ticketed concert audience in U.S. history.

title: ‘Harry Potter and the Cursed Child’ Celebrates 10 Years as Longest-Running Two-Part Play in Modern West End History – Global Bulletin
description:
DISTINGUISHED DECADE	

	“Harry Potter and the Cursed Child” turns 10 at London’s Palace Theatre today, July 30, cementing its place as the longest-
body:
DISTINGUISHED DECADE	

	“Harry Potter and the Cursed Child” turns 10 at London’s Palace Theatre today, July 30, cementing its place as the longest-running play in modern West End history to be performed as a two-part theatrical experience. Produced by Sonia Friedman Productions, Colin Callender and Harry Potter Theatrical Productions, the production has been seen by more than 2.5 million people at the Palace Theatre since opening in 2016 – over 300,000 of them first-time theatregoers. Across 1,762 combined performances of Part 1 and Part 2, the show has logged more than 8,300 hours on stage, with 276 cast members having appeared in the production and 45 making their professional debut. 
	

	Globally, the play has reached more than 14 million people across five current productions in London, New York, Tokyo, the Netherlands and a North American tour, and has collected a record 60 major awards, including nine Laurence Olivier Awards — the highest total ever awarded to a play – and six Tony Awards. Playwright Jack Thorne said: “Creating ‘Harry Potter and the Cursed Child’ has been a truly wonderful experience, and we are all delighted to be celebrating 10 years in the West End.” The original two-part production runs at the Palace Theatre until Sept. 20. A reimagined one-part version begins Oct. 9.

	
		ARTIFICIAL AMBITION	

	Yash Raj Films and Google will co-host an AI filmmaking workshop for India’s creative and production community on Aug. 4 at YRF Studios in Mumbai, giving participants hands-on training with Flow, Google’s AI creative studio. Among the first events to place Google’s Flow team inside a major international studio environment, the session will focus on integrating AI tools into existing production workflows while keeping creative control with filmmakers. Optional deep-dive modules and networking with Google’s AI engineering and product teams are also on offer. Akshaye Widhani, CEO of Yash Raj Films, said: “We’re choosing to have that conversation early and on our terms, in the room with the people building this technology.” Dr. Arathi Sethumadhavan, director, user experience research, technology & society, Google, said: “We are already seeing incredible momentum with Google Flow in India.”
	
	
		SARAWAK SPOTLIGHT	

	KC Global Media Asia has unveiled “AXN Ultimate Challenge: Sarawak,” a four-episode adventure competition series produced in partnership with AXN Asia and the Sarawak Tourism Board. Each 15-minute episode follows two content creator teams – Khenji Saito and Adam Samuel, and Estelle Fly and Saffron Sharpe – competing in challenges drawn from Sarawak’s landscapes and culture, with local figures including Chef Achang Libat and Blowpipe Masters Cikgu Nyoging and Alfa lending authenticity to the series. The show is hosted by Mark O’Dea and produced by KCGM Studios. It premieres on the AXN Asia YouTube channel July 31, followed by the AXN Taiwan YouTube channel on Aug. 4, and begins its linear run on AXN East Asia, AXN Singapore and AXN China on Aug. 4. George Chien, KC Global Media’s co-founder, president and CEO, said: “We look forward to audiences across the world becoming inspired to experience Sarawak for themselves.”

title: Arkansas Motorist Killed After Plowing Into Portable Toilet During Freak Accident
description:

                          Killed By Portable Toilet
body:
Arkansas Driver
                          Killed By Portable Toilet
                      
                  
                                                                        Published 
                              July 30, 2026
                            5:45 AM PDT
                                                                      |
                                                                Updated 
                                  July 30, 2026
                                6:37 AM PDT
                                    
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            A man in Arkansas was killed last week after his car hit a portable toilet during a freak accident.
      
    
            Ronald Langley was driving along Interstate 49 in Bentonville, AR, on the afternoon of July 24, along with a truck carrying two portable toilets, according to the Arkansas Department of Public Safety.
      
    
            One of the toilets suddenly tumbled off the truck into the roadway -- and Langley's Honda struck it, police said. As a result, cops say, Langley suffered fatal injuries, although it was unclear how the injuries were sustained.
      

                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            Langley's family has set up a GoFundMe to help with funeral expenses and other costs. On the GoFundMe page, the fundraiser says Langley took every precaution but still died in a highway accident because of someone else's negligence, leaving "his wife without a breadwinner."
      
    
            Ronald was 56.

            Ian Diaz from "A Toxic Love Story" has remarried since framing his ex in a cyberstalking hoax ... tying the knot with an old girlfriend, TMZ has learned.
      
    
            Sources close to Ian tell TMZ ... Ian had dated a woman named Amy before he dated Michelle Hadley and married Angela Connell Diaz, and they got hitched before the cyber scandal unfolded.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            Our sources tell us Ian and Amy secretly married in 2020 ... before he was sentenced to prison. We're also told Ian's fathered children with Amy ... although it's unclear if that happened when they dated initially or since they got married.
      

            The sources did say Amy and Ian maintained a friendship after they broke up and she comforted him when Ian discovered Angela was never pregnant with twins.
      
    
            As you know, Ian and Angela wound up behind bars after they allegedly framed Michelle for outlandish crimes ... like trying to arrange for Angela to get raped via a Craigslist ad.
      
    
            Authorities arrested Angela in January 2017, and Ian annulled their marriage that April. He wasn't arrested until 2021.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            Our sources say Amy's been Ian's biggest supporter, and tell us she believes Ian is innocent and was not part of the emails.
      
    
            In 2023, Ian was sentenced to 10+ years in prison for conspiracy to commit cyberstalking, perjury, and obstruction of a federal matter.

title: Jared Leto Sexual Assault Allegation Not Reported to Las Vegas Police
description:
Jared Leto
                          Vegas Sex Assault Allegation Never Reported
body:
Jared Leto
                          Vegas Sex Assault Allegation Never Reported
                      
                  
                                                                        Published 
                              July 29, 2026
                            5:15 PM PDT
                                                                            
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            Las Vegas police say they have no sexual assault reports involving Jared Leto ... following a new BBC documentary featuring a woman who alleges the actor assaulted her in the city when she was 17.
      
    
            A spokesperson for the Las Vegas Metropolitan Police Department tells TMZ ... "There have been no sexual assault reports filed against this individual in LVMPD’s jurisdiction."
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            In the Vegas allegation, a woman claims Leto sexually assaulted her inside a motel bathroom after they met at a local store in 2002.
      

            As we reported, four women accused Leto of sexual assault or threatening sexual assault when they were teenagers. The claims include an alleged encounter with a 17-year-old in California, an alleged threat against a 19-year-old in London, and accusations that he groomed a girl through sexually explicit phone calls beginning when she was 16.
      
    
            The BBC investigation details allegations tied to Vegas, California, and London between 2002 and 2016. We've reached out to the Los Angeles Police Department, the Los Angeles County Sheriff's Department, and London's Metropolitan Police to ask whether any reports have been filed or investigations opened involving Leto ... so far, no word back.
      
    
            Leto denies ever sexually assaulting anyone, previously telling TMZ ... "I have never sexually assaulted anyone in my entire life. These claims are absolutely and categorically false."
